definitions.gloss: wood ear mushroom, cloud ear fungus
definitions.explanation: A dark, ear-shaped edible fungus with a crunchy, gelatinous texture. Commonly used in stir-fries and ramen.

examples.japanese: ⟦ラーメン→ラーメン：05181_raamen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧キクラゲ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧のせる。
examples.english: To put wood ear mushrooms on ramen.

examples.japanese: キクラゲ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦コリコリ→コリコリ：06846_korikori⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{食感|しょっかん}→食感：06636_shokkan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: Wood ear mushrooms have a nice crunchy texture.

examples.japanese: ⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧キクラゲ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{戻|もど}して→戻す：02317_modosu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Dried wood ear mushrooms are rehydrated in water before using in stir-fries.

notes:
WRITING:
Usually written in katakana as キクラゲ. The kanji {木耳|きくらげ} (literally "tree ear") exists but is rarely used.

ETYMOLOGY:
The name comes from ⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧ (tree) + クラゲ (jellyfish), because the fungus grows on trees and has a jellyfish-like texture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧キクラゲ: dried wood ear mushroom
- キクラゲ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧: stir-fried wood ear mushrooms
- キクラゲ{入|い}り⟦ラーメン→ラーメン：05181_raamen⟧: ramen with wood ear mushrooms
